chunks: And Isma'il ibn Sa'd asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام:
About a man who swears an oath while his intention is upon something other than what he swore; he said: "The oath is according to the intention."

key_terms.الضَّمِيرِ: the inward intention upon which the oath rests
key_terms.بِالْيَمِينِ: by an oath; the formal act of swearing
key_terms.ضَمِيرُهُ: his inward intention or inner meaning

ai.seo_question: In Shia hadith, is an oath judged by its wording or by the person's intention?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the legal consideration of an oath is tied to the inward intention behind it. It highlights the importance of niyyah and indicates that the meaning of an oath is determined by what the person intended.
